source_snippet: 13.118.010 Definitions. As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires: "County resident" refers to any individual whose primary and legal place of residence is located within the geographical boundaries of Storey County. Residency may be demonstrated through documentation such as a valid driver’s license or state ID with a Storey County address, a current utility bill, lease or mortgage agreement, voter registration, or other official documents showing name and address within the Storey County. “Immediate Family” means the Storey County Resident’s spouse or domestic partner, parents, children (including stepchildren and legally adopted children), siblings, grandparents, and grandchildren, whether related by blood, marriage, or legal adoption. source_snippet: 4. Staff summary: This resolution is in recognition of the lifesaving efforts made by Storey County Fire District Firefighter Jesse Richardson. On July 26th Jesse responded along with his partner Charlie Bowman to a fire on Lousetown Road with a report of a victim trapped. While Charlie attempted access to the interior of the structure, Jesse carried a 24’ ladder around to the C side of the structure locating the victim on the balcony. He placed the ladder and even utilized a rock to stabilize it due to the angle. He then ascended the ladder and assisted the resident over the railing and down to safety. Without his efforts, the outcome could have been fatal.

The dominant asset is the Pumpkin Hollow copper project, located approximately 7 miles southeast of Yerington within 22,862 acres in Mason Valley. Following the June 2024 bankruptcy of Nevada Copper Corp., the Pumpkin Hollow assets were acquired by Southwest Critical Materials LLC, an affiliate of Kinterra Capital, in a $128 million 363 sale completed October 2024. In September 2025, Kinterra announced plans to restart copper production within 24 months, securing $80 million in equity financing led by Lionhead. source_snippet: 3.5 Healthcare & Social Services Health Care & Social Assistance employed 324 workers in 2025, though this represents a decline of 27 jobs (−7.8%) from 2020. The sector is significantly underrepresented relative to national averages (LQ = 0.71), indicating that Yerington residents likely travel to Carson City, Reno, or other centers for many healthcare services. Banner Churchill Community Hospital in Fallon and Renown/Saint Mary’s systems in Reno serve as referral destinations. Given the area’s rapidly aging population (47% aged 55+) and the national retirement wave, healthcare capacity will be an increasingly pressing issue. Gaps in primary care, behavioral health, dental services, and elder care represent both community need and economic development opportunity. Healthcare practitioners earn a median hourly wage of $43.47—the highest of any occupational group in the area.

The primary objective of the Community Development Block Grant Program is the development of viable communities by providing: i. expanding economic opportunities principally for persons of low and moderate income, ii. suitable living environments, and iii. decent housing. Funds granted through this program support community development activities directed toward the following objectives stated in Title I of HCDA of 1974, as amended.

As a result, the 100-year alternative was not pursued further, and a 25-year culvert improvement alternative was developed. The existing 10-foot by 6-foot box culvert under SR 341 (Occidental Grade) is undersized and flow overtops the roadway in both the 25-year and 100-year storm events. Because SR 342 is classified by NDOT as a Major Collector, the culvert crossing may be designed for the 25-year event. Executive Summary This report provides the Board of County Commissioners with a comprehensive update on code enforcement actions taken with respect to the property located at [address redacted], Dayton, Nevada (Assessor's Parcel Number 016-151-14). Over a period of approximately ten months, Lyon County Code Enforcement Division, in collaboration with multiple partner agencies, successfully facilitated the complete remediation and cleanup of the subject property. The operation proceeded lawfully, safely, and in full accordance with the coordinated plan developed by participating agencies.

Background In June 2025, the Lyon County Code Enforcement Division initiated formal contact with the owners of Parcel 016-151-14 regarding conditions identified on the subject property that posed public health risks, safety hazards, and environmental concerns, and which had generated increasing community complaints. The Division issued written correspondence to the property owner notifying them of the situation and requesting their engagement in developing a coordinated and lawful course of action. That initial correspondence marked the beginning of an extensive ten-month collaborative effort between Lyon County Code Enforcement and the property ownership group. Notice to Vacate Operations On Thursday, April 16, 2026, the Lyon County Code Enforcement Officer, assisted by deputies from the Lyon County Sheriff's Office, conducted formal posting and personal service of Notices to Vacate throughout the subject property. Prior to the issuance of notices, the property owner had executed a trespass order through the Lyon County Sheriff's Office, which authorized the condensed 48-hour notice period afforded to occupants to vacate the premises in accordance with applicable legal requirements. Upon expiration of the notice period at 2:00 p.m. on Saturday, April 18, 2026, deputies from the Lyon County Sheriff's Office responded to the site. It was observed that the majority of individuals had already voluntarily departed the property prior to the deadline. The remaining occupants also vacated the premises voluntarily. plain_language_summary: 8. Preserve Historic and Scenic Character Downtown Downtown development must be consistent with Carson City’s unique historic identity and scale. Large block-style buildings will erode visibility of our scenic surroundings.
